answer.label: A documented user, not the originator
answer.sourceLine: Susan Sontag is recorded using this saying in Charles Ruas’s 1982 profile. It was already in print in 1976, according to Quote Investigator’s documented research, so the evidence supports her use rather than a claim that she invented it.

source.heading: The source

Alix Nelson and Ross Macdonald, 1976, documented by QI

source.excerpt: Writing well is the best revenge.
trail: The reproduced Ruas profile ↗ describes Sontag saying the line while discussing attacks on her political remarks.
Quote Investigator’s research ↗ supplies earlier 1976 examples and the full bibliographical citation for the 1982 profile.

Anne Ruggles Gere’s own publication list records a 1978 article with the saying as its title, independently establishing another use before Sontag’s 1982 profile; the article itself was not inspected.
source.rightsNote: The quoted English phrase is documented in modern copyrighted publications. The brief identifying excerpt does not reproduce the surrounding interview.

author.name: Susan Sontag
author.heading: About Susan Sontag
author.bio: Susan Sontag wrote criticism, fiction and essays about photography, illness, art and politics. Her collections Against Interpretation and On Photography made her a prominent public intellectual, while her political interventions frequently drew public argument.

cite.sourceCitation: Ruas, Charles. “Susan Sontag: Past, Present and Future.” New York Times Book Review, 24 October 1982, p. 11; reproduced online. Earlier uses documented by Quote Investigator.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘Writing well is the best revenge’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

copyAttribution: Used by Susan Sontag in a 1982 Charles Ruas profile; the saying is documented earlier in 1976. Original coiner unknown.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In the profile, Sontag is discussing the hostile response to her comments about communism and her desire to return to writing a novel. The quip expresses a response to that immediate controversy, but its earlier printed appearances make it unsafe to present it as a saying she coined.

schema.claimReviewed: Susan Sontag originated the saying “Writing well is the best revenge.”
schema.faqAnswer: Susan Sontag is documented using the saying in 1982, but she did not originate its documented wording: Quote Investigator records uses in 1976. The original coiner remains unknown.
schema.verdictNote: This verdict concerns origination, not Sontag’s genuine reported use.
